title: Walsh character of the small-bias generator
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\ell$ be a nonzero natural number, and let $\gamma\colon \{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb F_2$, where $\mathbb F_2$ is the field with two elements. For $r,s$ in the degree-$\ell$ extension field of $\mathbb F_2$, let $P_\gamma(X)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\gamma_iX^{i+1}$, with coefficients viewed in that extension field, and encode its elements as binary vectors using a fixed $\mathbb F_2$-linear isomorphism with $\mathbb F_2^\ell$. The Walsh character indexed by $\gamma$, evaluated at the vector whose $i$th coordinate is the binary dot product of the encodings of $r^{i+1}$ and $s$, equals the Walsh character indexed by the encoding of $P_\gamma(r)$, evaluated at the encoding of $s$.
hypotheses_covered: $r$ and $s$ belong to the degree-$\ell$ binary extension field
